title: Reverse Hom comparisons and compose component naturality squares
statement: For categories A,B and bifunctors HA:A.op product A -> A, HB:B.op product B -> B, a comparison HB followed by an equivalence E:B≌A with its two-variable transport determines the reverse comparison along E.inverse. Also, a functor F sends any commuting square f followed by e prime = e followed by g to a commuting square. Composing this with a second square F(g) followed by i prime = i followed by h gives the naturality of F.mapIso(e) followed by i. All isomorphisms and equations are specified, not chosen.

source.place: Equivalence.unitIso, counitIso and trans; NatIso.op, NatIso.prod, and the whiskering isomorphisms; Hom-comparison application motivated by Stacks 03EO.

proof.text: Whisker the forward comparison with E.inverse in each argument and its value; cancel the forward functor by the counit in the arguments and by the unit in the value. This is inverseHomComparison.
Expand the hom of a composite isomorphism. Use F.map_comp to map the first given square, then reassociate and substitute the second square. This gives mapIso_comp_naturality.

lean.statement:
def inverseHomComparison {A B : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] (E : B ≌ A)
    (HA : Aᵒᵖ × A ⥤ A) (HB : Bᵒᵖ × B ⥤ B)
    (h : HB ⋙ E.functor ≅ E.functor.op.prod E.functor ⋙ HA) :
    HA ⋙ E.inverse ≅ E.inverse.op.prod E.inverse ⋙ HB
